description_full: VSE Corporation engages in providing aviation aftermarket parts distribution and maintenance, repair, and overhaul services for air transportation assets for commercial and government markets. It offers its services to global client base of commercial airlines, regional airlines, air cargo transporters, MRO integrators and providers, aviation manufacturers, corporate and private aircraft owners, and fixed-base operators. The company was incorporated in 1959 and is headquartered in Miramar, Florida.
ceo_bio: Mr. John A. Cuomo J.D. | CEO, President & Director | Age 51 | Compensation: $3.5M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 1K people. Revenue per employee of $695K ranks in the top quartile among Industrials peers. Each employee generates $4K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $8K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 5× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (2/10).
financial_summary: VSE Corporation is a mid-cap industrials business with a $4.9B market cap on $1.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years and +8% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $6M in free cash flow — roughly 1 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.31× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.7× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 4.4×.
Net dilution runs at 8.9% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
